stories.title: Helen Toner says the public still can't trust AI company CEOs
stories.summary: In a podcast interview, former OpenAI board member Helen Toner argues the public still cannot fully trust AI CEOs, drawing on her experience from the 2023 effort to remove Sam Altman.
stories.more: The interview, part of a Verge podcast series on AI in real life, features Toner in her current role as executive director of Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology. She is best known for having sat on OpenAI's board during the 2023 attempt to oust CEO Sam Altman, an episode the conversation revisits as context for her views on AI governance. The excerpt does not detail what new evidence or arguments she raises beyond the framing that trust in AI leadership remains unresolved.

stories.title: Wired warns of a rising wave of AI-assisted ransomware attacks
stories.summary: Wired reports that while fully automated ransomware doesn't exist yet, attackers with limited technical skill are increasingly using AI tools to carry out more damaging ransomware campaigns.
stories.more: The article's framing is that AI is lowering the skill floor for ransomware operators rather than creating a wholly new, autonomous threat. According to the excerpt, attackers described as "unsophisticated" are nonetheless able to "wreak havoc" by leaning on AI tools to fill gaps in their own technical ability. Specific techniques, targets, or incidents are not detailed in the available excerpt.

items.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
items.excerpt: Fully automated ransomware hasn’t arrived—yet. But seemingly unsophisticated attackers are using AI tools to wreak havoc.

stories.title: r/LocalLLaMA debates how long open models can keep pace at ~100B+ sizes
stories.summary: A r/LocalLLaMA thread questions how long the community can rely on a handful of labs for capable open models, as frontier open releases grow toward 300B+ parameters.
stories.more: The poster estimates current open models in the 25–200B range from makers like Qwen, Gemma, and Nvidia should remain viable for consumer hardware through roughly 2027, but expects that window to close as more labs push toward 300B and eventually 500B parameter models. They cite examples including DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 at 284B and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at 552B (with a 196B active/engaged variant), arguing such sizes no longer fit comfortably on unified 128GB memory setups or a 128GB RAM plus 24–32GB VRAM combination even at Q4 quantization. The underlying concern is a shrinking supply of open-weight models that run well on consumer-grade hardware. The thread does not reach a conclusion on what, if anything, the community should do about it.

stories.title: Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia CEO ripples through Asian chip markets
stories.summary: Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia's CEO is prompting reactions across Asia, with some governments confirming chip supply commitments while others watch for fallout on local projects.
stories.more: TechCrunch reports that Asian governments are responding to Huang's exit in different ways: some are moving quickly to lock in existing chip supply agreements, while others are monitoring how the leadership change might affect local AI and semiconductor projects, and a few are addressing related ongoing investigations. The Verge frames Huang's departure as the end of an era for the industry's visionary showman-founder CEO archetype, pointing back to his triumphant January 2025 keynote appearance before a 14,000-person crowd as emblematic of that style of leadership. Neither Source's excerpt specifies the exact date or stated reason for Huang's exit, or who succeeds him as CEO.

stories.title: OpenAI again disbands its standalone robotics team
stories.summary: OpenAI is dissolving its dedicated robotics team for the second time, reassigning researchers to other teams as it bets general-purpose models can control robots directly.
stories.more: According to The Decoder, OpenAI frames the move as an effort to accelerate its robotics work overall rather than retreat from it, redistributing the team's researchers across other groups. The company's reasoning is that general-purpose models, cited as "GPT-6 Astra," can apparently control robots directly, reducing the need for a specialized robotics unit. The article notes this is the second time OpenAI has dissolved a standalone robotics team. It does not specify team size, timeline, or which teams are absorbing the researchers.
